_comment: Rhode Island 2026 QAP, RIHousing. Competitive scoring criteria. The source PDF is a scan with no text layer; this extraction reads the OCR'd copy, and page numbers are PDF page indices in that file. Where OCR mangled a point value, the value was read off the rendered page image and cross-checked against the Scoring/Point Allocation Summary table on p.32; those criteria carry a note saying so.

track_totals.note: The Scoring/Point Allocation Summary table on p.32 totals 147 points: Financing 60, Incomes/Populations Served 44, Promoting RI Workforce/Permitting 16, Community 13, Sustainability 14. Up to 20 negative points may also be assessed. Note the QAP contradicts itself: the section header on p.33 reads 'FINANCING POINTS (Up to 66 points)' while the summary table and the itemised maxima (25+20+5+10) both give 60.

groups.label: Community category (Housing 2030)
groups.source_quote: applicants are only eligible for one category and a maximum of 10
groups.note: The three Housing 2030 community categories are alternatives worth 10, 7 and 5 points. Only one may be claimed, capped at 10.

criteria.heading: TDC per residential unit
criteria.quote: TDC per residential unit based on construction type as defined
criteria.note: Scored on a Weighted Average TDC, ([2 * TDC/unit] + [TDC/# of bedrooms]) / 3, in $5,000 increments against a maximum per building type published in the Developer's Handbook rather than in the QAP. Extraordinary conditions (pp.34-35) may be deducted before scoring.
